PrivacyEe.lead: What data the Estonian pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Personal Data Protection Act (isikuandmete kaitse seadus, IKS).

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The provider named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of provider accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about healthcare providers
body: Data: the provider’s name as the Health Board’s register publishes it, the numbers and kinds of its activity licences, the kind of hospital where it is one, the services it is licensed for, and the addresses of its places of activity; for a pharmacy, its name, its State Agency of Medicines licence number, its address and its telephone number. A provider that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Never stored, although the sources publish them: the health workers the register names with each provider (their codes, names, professions and specialties), the provider’s Business Register code and legal address, and, for a pharmacy, the name of its responsible pharmacist, its e-mail address, its fax number and the name of its licence holder. A telephone number that the pharmacies’ register gives for more than three pharmacies is a chain’s and is not shown.

Identifier: a provider’s page ends with the number of its first activity licence in force (for example l01909 for licence L01909), a pharmacy’s with its place of business code at the State Agency of Medicines (for example ap457).

Purpose: letting the public find a healthcare provider or a pharmacy, what it is licensed for, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.
Retention: as long as the provider or pharmacy appears in its register. A page disappears when the register no longer lists it; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the providers themselves (GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would involve a disproportionate effort (article 14(5)(b)); this notice, the data page and a notice on every page make the information public.

people.heading: Providers, and the people they name
body: An Estonian page is a healthcare provider or a pharmacy, never a person’s profile: the health workers registered with each provider are not listed. Some providers are sole traders (füüsilisest isikust ettevõtja, FIE) whose business name is their own name; the page shows that name as the register publishes it, as a professional detail, with the provider’s activity licences, places of activity and services. The categories of data concerned are those listed above; their source is the Health Board’s register (MEDRE open data); their recipient is the public.

Nothing else about any person is collected: no personal identification code, no Business Register code, no private address, no e-mail, no ratings and no reviews. No patient’s data, and no health data, is processed by the directory.
Anyone a page is about can object to it at any time, and the page is removed.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Healthcare providers come from the Health Board’s open data on providers and their activity licences (Tervishoiuteenuse osutajate ning tegevuslubade andmestik), kept in the MEDRE information system run by the Health and Welfare Information Systems Centre (TEHIK) and published under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Pharmacies come from the State Agency of Medicines’ register of activity licences (CC0 1.0). Places come from the Land and Spatial Development Board’s administrative and settlement units, and addresses from its address data system (CC0 1.0). Each source is credited as it asks:

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: patients need to know which healthcare providers and pharmacies are licensed where, what they are licensed for and how to reach them, a need the State already meets by publishing these registers for public use.

Necessity: only the provider’s data from the registers is shown, data the registers publish anyway, and less of it: no health worker is listed, no e-mail, no Business Register code; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews.

Balance: a professional context, factual information, a neutral order, no advertising, the minimum of the registers’ fields, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every update of the registers. A sole trader holding an activity licence, listed by name in a public register, expects to be found in a directory repeating that information. Weighing these points, the interests of patients prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Provider accounts and claims
body: Data: e-mail address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the provider or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right provider. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact e-mail address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is my page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a provider that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in providers and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; provider sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, under a contract that meets GDPR article 28. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Union
body: Data is transferred outside the European Union and the European Economic Area only under the safeguards of chapter V of the GDPR (an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses). Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can also lodge a complaint with the Data Protection Inspectorate (Andmekaitse Inspektsioon), Estonia’s supervisory authority (GDPR article 77), or with the supervisory authority of the country where you live or work.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the registers never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

changes.heading: Updates to this notice
body: This notice is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer admitted in Estonia and by the data protection officer; every version is dated.

TermsEe.metaDescription: Terms of use of the Estonian pages of Apercura: a free, factual directory of licensed healthcare providers and pharmacies from public registers, without booking.
TermsEe.title: Terms of use
TermsEe.lead: The rules for using the Estonian pages of Apercura, for the public and for healthcare providers alike.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura lists, free of charge, the healthcare providers that hold an activity licence in the Health Board’s register and the general pharmacies of the State Agency of Medicines’ register. It lists providers, not the health workers who work for them. It is a directory only: no appointment is booked through Apercura in Estonia. It is run by the provider named in the legal notice.
Using the directory requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from public registers, as they publish it, in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement. A provider’s page prints its activity licence numbers, as the Advertising Act requires.

The information may be incomplete or out of date, and a place of activity whose address the address data system does not know is shown at its settlement, not at its exact address on a map: check the information with the provider before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 112. The family doctors’ advice line answers at 1220.

providers.heading: For healthcare providers
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant runs the provider or acts for it, checked by a person before the page is handed over.

The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date: the Advertising Act (§ 22) prohibits advertising of health services, and only facts such as the provider’s name, opening hours, place of activity, specialty, services and prices may be published.

removal.heading: Removing a page
body: Anyone a page is about can ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information providers add to their pages. These limits will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The Health Board’s data is republished under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: anyone may reuse it from these pages under that licence, non-commercially, with the credit and under the same licence. The State Agency of Medicines’ and the address data are under CC0 1.0, the administrative units under the Land and Spatial Development Board’s open data licence.

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: These terms are governed by Estonian law; the mandatory consumer protection rules of the country of residence always apply. The competent court will be specified during the legal review. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution.

AccessibilityEe.metaDescription: Accessibility of the Estonian pages of Apercura: the WCAG 2.2 AA target, what was checked, what remains, and how to report a problem.
AccessibilityEe.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityEe.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the Estonian pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: The Products and Services Accessibility Act (toodete ja teenuste ligipääsetavuse seadus, LPS) covers e-commerce and the other services it lists, not a free directory, and the web accessibility rules of the Public Information Act bind public bodies. Apercura’s provider nevertheless aims at the same standard on every page: WCAG 2.2 level AA (EN 301 549).

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The Estonian pages share the code of the other markets’ pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress.

tests.heading: What was checked
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers, in Estonian.
A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages, including the Estonian texts.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within one month and, where needed, give you the information in another form.

status.heading: Last update
status.body: The Health Board publishes its register every day and the State Agency of Medicines keeps its register up to date; the directory reads them every week and imports a register when it has changed. A page changes only when its facts change in its register.
status.notImported: The Estonian directory has not been imported yet on this site.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.body: The Health Board publishes its register of healthcare providers under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported licence (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), the State Agency of Medicines its register of activity licences and the Land and Spatial Development Board its address data under CC0 1.0, and the Board its administrative and settlement units as open data to be credited with their date. Each credit below is printed word for word.

ee-medre.use: Healthcare providers: names, activity licences (numbers and kinds), kinds of hospital, licensed services, addresses of the places of activity
ee-medre.frequency: Every day, by the Health Board

ee-ehak.frequency: Every month, by the Land and Spatial Development Board

sources.maru: Land and Spatial Development Board’s open data licence

licence.heading: The licence of the Estonian data
body: The Health Board’s data is reused under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 Unported, and the Estonian data as republished on these pages (the providers’ pages, their listings and their sitemaps) is available under the same licence, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: anyone may reuse it from here, with the credit, for a non-commercial purpose and under the same licence. No other licence claim of the site covers it: the AGPL-3.0 licence covers Apercura’s source code, not this data.
list: Non-commercial (licence § 4(c)): Apercura is free for patients and for providers, run without profit, open source (AGPL-3.0), with no advertising, no paid ranking or placement and no sale or rental of data. Its use of the register is not primarily intended for or directed toward commercial advantage or private monetary compensation.

Share-alike (licence § 4(b)): what Apercura adds to the register (the places and points of the Land and Spatial Development Board, the pharmacies) does not change the licence of the Health Board’s data, which stays CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 wherever it is shown. The State Agency of Medicines’ and the address data stay under CC0 1.0, the administrative units under the Land and Spatial Development Board’s open data licence, with their credit.
Credit (licence § 4(d)): every page built from the register names the Health Board, the dataset and the licence, and says that the data was changed.
The Health Board has been asked to confirm this reading; the pages are published meanwhile, and will follow its answer.

Each place of activity is placed at its address point in the address data system, else at its settlement’s centre; names are shown as the register writes them, without their legal form (OÜ, AS, SA…) and in ordinary case when the register writes them in capitals.

coverage.heading: Providers covered
body: Pages are generated for every healthcare provider that holds an activity licence in the Health Board’s register and has a place of activity open to patients, and for the general pharmacies of the State Agency of Medicines’ register, branches included. A provider is listed once, under the first kind its licences give: a hospital, a family practice, a dental clinic, another provider of specialist care, then nursing care (nursing hospitals included), midwifery, physiotherapy, clinical psychology and speech therapy. Every licence, with its number, and every service is shown on the page.

Not listed: the health workers registered with each provider and the family doctors’ lists, which name people; providers whose only licences are ambulance services; the places of school health services; hospital and veterinary pharmacies, which do not serve the public.

A place of activity is placed at its address point in the address data system (Maa- ja Ruumiamet). An address the system does not know is placed at the centre of its settlement: its map position and its distance are then those of the settlement, never of the address.

kinds.EE_NURSING: Nursing care (home nursing, nurses’ practices, nursing hospitals)

/ee/asutus/naidisapteek-ap457: a pharmacy (ap) and its place of business code at the State Agency of Medicines.

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the registers: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: Healthcare providers: the provider applies to the Health Board to amend its activity licence (a new place of activity, a new service), and the register carries the change.
Pharmacies: the licence holder reports the change to the State Agency of Medicines.

A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space.

No appointment is booked through Apercura in Poland. The individual and group practices of doctors, dentists, nurses and midwives are not listed.

body: The person below is responsible for what the service provider publishes. Information an establishment adds to its own page is its own responsibility; as a service that stores information provided by its users, the provider answers for it only under the conditions of article 14 of the Act of 18 July 2002 on providing services by electronic means.

body: The directory is built from the register of entities performing medical activity (Rejestr Podmiotów Wykonujących Działalność Leczniczą, RPWDL), which Centrum e-Zdrowia publishes on dane.gov.pl under CC BY 4.0. The register is public by law (article 106(1a) of the Act of 15 April 2011 on medical activity: “Rejestr jest jawny.”). It can be incomplete or out of date: check the information with the establishment before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

body: Article 14(1) of the Act of 15 April 2011 on medical activity asks every provider of medical activity to make public the scope and kinds of the health services it provides, and says that the content and form of that information must not have the features of advertising. That duty binds the providers, about their own information.

Apercura is not a provider of medical activity and is paid by no one for a page. It publishes the same facts, from the public register, for every establishment and in the same form: name, kind, cells, address, telephone. No ranking, no rating, no review, no paid placement, no promotional wording; listings follow a neutral order. An establishment that claims its page may add factual information only (a presentation, languages, opening hours), under the same rule.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code of Apercura is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The directory data is reused under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0): the data page lists every source with the attribution it requires, and the times of production and of obtaining of the register’s data.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura lists, free of charge, the healthcare establishments of the register of entities performing medical activity (RPWDL) that patients visit: hospitals, outpatient and specialist clinics, dental clinics, rehabilitation, nurses and midwives, laboratories, hospices, care and treatment homes, sanatoria and addiction treatment centres. It is a directory only: no appointment is booked through Apercura in Poland. It is provided by the service provider named in the legal notice.

The services provided electronically are: browsing and searching the directory, reporting an error, objecting to a page, asking for contact, and, for an establishment, an account to claim and complete its page. Browsing requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from the public register, in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement.
The information may be incomplete or out of date: check it with the establishment before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 112 or 999. Outside clinic hours, night and holiday care (nocna i świąteczna opieka zdrowotna) can help; the National Health Fund’s helpline is 800 190 590.

practices.heading: For healthcare establishments
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant runs the establishment or acts for it, checked by a person before the page is handed over.

The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date, and must not have the features of advertising (article 14 of the Act of 15 April 2011 on medical activity).

removal.heading: Removing a page
body: Anyone a page names or is about can ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

technical.heading: Technical requirements
body: A device with an Internet connection and an up-to-date web browser is enough; JavaScript is needed for the forms and the establishment space only. An establishment account needs an e-mail address. Like any service provided over the Internet, the site carries the usual risks of the network; the provider protects it with encrypted connections and encrypts the documents and free text sent to it.

unlawful.heading: Unlawful content
body: Users must not provide unlawful content: false information, content that infringes the rights of others, advertising of medical activity, or malicious code. Such content is removed, and an account used for it may be closed.

complaints.heading: Complaints
body: A complaint about the service can be sent to the address below, saying what is wrong and how to reach you. The provider answers within 14 days.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information establishments add to their pages. These limits will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. Directory data is reused under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0).

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: The governing law and the competent courts will be specified during the legal review; the mandatory consumer protection rules of the country of residence always apply. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution.

AccessibilityPl.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the Polish pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: The Act of 4 April 2019 on the digital accessibility of websites and mobile applications of public bodies binds public bodies (article 2), which Apercura is not. Its service provider nevertheless aims at the same standard on every page, WCAG 2.2 level AA, and follows the structure of the statement that article 10 of that Act asks for.

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The Polish pages share the code of the other markets’ pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress.

tests.heading: How it was assessed
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers, in Polish.
A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages.

other.heading: Premises, sign language and mobile application
body: Apercura has no premises open to the public and no mobile application. It offers no Polish Sign Language interpreter; write to the address below and you will get the information in another form.

feedback.heading: Report a lack of accessibility
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within one month and, where needed, give you the information in another form.

coverage.heading: Establishments covered
body: Pages are generated for the healthcare establishments (zakłady lecznicze) of the healthcare entities (podmioty lecznicze) that are active on the day of the import, from the kind of activity of each establishment (hospital, other inpatient care, outpatient care) and the kinds of its active cells (part VIII of the ministry’s identification codes). A specialist clinic of one or two fields is listed under the more specific one; a clinic of three fields or more as a specialist clinic.

Left out: establishments whose cells are only school nurses, emergency medical teams, sanitary transport or blood banks; closed or suspended establishments, units and cells. Not listed at all: the individual and group practices of doctors, dentists, nurses and midwives (praktyki zawodowe), until a legal opinion on listing named practitioners (the Supreme Administrative Court’s case III OSK 1052/21), and pharmacies: the pharmacy register is open under CC BY 4.0, but it is published only as a legacy spreadsheet and names owners and managers, so it is planned for later.

An establishment run by a natural person is shown under its establishment’s name, with that person’s name taken out where the register allows it to be recognised; the entity’s own name, which is the person’s, is never shown.
Every place is located at the point of its gmina: the register publishes addresses, no coordinates, so distances are approximate and pages show no map pin.

provider.heading: Service provider (ehandelsloven § 8)
body: The Norwegian pages of Apercura are provided by the entity below: its name, its address, its e-mail address and the other details that let you reach it directly, the register that keeps it and its organisation number, and whether it is registered for VAT. It runs the directory and answers for its content.

The provider is established in another state of the European Economic Area: under section 5 of the E-Commerce Act, its service follows the rules of that state within the coordinated field, and this notice gives the information Norwegian law asks for as well.

service.heading: The service
body: A free directory of Norway’s hospitals, mental health and addiction treatment services, GP offices, emergency clinics (legevakt), specialist practices, dental clinics, nursing homes and pharmacies, built from the establishments that the Brønnøysund Register Centre’s Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (Enhetsregisteret) lists under a health or pharmacy industry code, without advertising, with a space where an establishment can complete its own page. Pages are establishments, never the health personnel who work in them. No appointment is booked through Apercura in Norway.

marketing.heading: Factual pages
body: Section 13 of the Health Personnel Act (helsepersonelloven) requires any marketing of health and care services, and of the undertakings that provide them, to be sound, sober and factual (“forsvarlig, nøktern og saklig”). The pages show facts from public registers (name, address, telephone number, organisation number, registered industry) in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement. An establishment that completes its page is bound by the same rule.

Information an establishment adds to its own page is its own responsibility; as a host of information provided by its users, the provider answers for it only under the conditions of section 18 of the E-Commerce Act and of the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, article 6).

liability.heading: Content of the pages

An establishment’s industry code is what it declared to the register, not a licence or an authorisation: the directory can be incomplete, out of date or list a unit that no longer receives patients. PrivacyNo.title: Privacy
PrivacyNo.lead: What data the Norwegian pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which applies in Norway through the EEA Agreement and the Personal Data Act (personopplysningsloven).

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The provider named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of establishment accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about establishments
body: Data: the establishment’s name, the address where it is located, its telephone number, its organisation number and the industry code it registered, as the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities publishes them, and, for an establishment run by a public body or a foundation, the name of that body. An establishment that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Never stored, although the register publishes them: the establishments of sole proprietorships (enkeltpersonforetak), whose name is their owner’s; establishments named after a doctor or a dentist (“Lege Ola Nordmann AS”); the care-of lines of an address; e-mail addresses, mobile numbers and websites; the number of employees; the roles of the register (managers, board members, owners). A telephone number the register gives for more than three establishments is a switchboard’s and is not shown.
Identifier: a page ends with the establishment’s organisation number in the register (for example 910000039), never a person’s national identity number.

Purpose: letting the public find a hospital, a GP office, a dental clinic, a nursing home or a pharmacy, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.

Retention: as long as the register lists the establishment under one of the industry codes read. A page disappears when the register no longer lists it, or when the establishment is closed or its owner enters bankruptcy or liquidation; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the establishments themselves (GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would involve a disproportionate effort (article 14(5)(b)); this notice, the data page and a notice on every page make the information public.

people.heading: Establishments, not people
body: A Norwegian page is an establishment, never a person’s profile: the health personnel who work in it are not listed, and the register’s roles are never read. The Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data does not cover personal data without a lawful basis for its further processing (NLOD 2.0, section 3), one more reason why the directory leaves out sole proprietorships, named after their owner, and the establishments named after a doctor or a dentist. The name of a company that holds a person’s name may still remain in another one; anyone it concerns can object, and the page is removed.

Nothing else about any person is collected: no national identity number, no private address, no e-mail, no ratings and no reviews. No patient’s data, and no health data, is processed by the directory.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Establishments come from the Brønnøysund Register Centre’s Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (Enhetsregisteret), published as open data under the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD 2.0); the owners’ legal form, read to leave out sole proprietorships, from the same register. Counties and municipalities come from Kartverket’s administrative divisions, and the points of the addresses from the cadastre’s addresses (Matrikkelen – Adresse), both under CC BY 4.0. Each source is credited as it asks:

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: patients need to know which hospitals, GP offices, dental clinics, nursing homes and pharmacies exist where and how to reach them, a need the State already meets by publishing the register for public use.

Necessity: only the establishment’s data from the register is shown, data the register publishes anyway, and less of it: no person is listed, no e-mail, no mobile number, no role; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews.

Balance: a professional context, factual information as section 13 of the Health Personnel Act asks, a neutral order, no advertising, the minimum of the register’s fields, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every update of the register. A company or a public body listed in a public register under a health industry code expects to be found in a directory repeating that information. Weighing these points, the interests of patients prevail, and anyone a page concerns can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Establishment accounts and claims
body: Data: e-mail address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the establishment or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right establishment. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact e-mail address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is my page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.

Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping an establishment that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in establishments and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; establishment sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, under a contract that meets GDPR article 28. Data is hosted in the European Economic Area. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Economic Area
body: Data is transferred outside the European Economic Area only under the safeguards of chapter V of the GDPR (an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses). Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can also lodge a complaint with the Norwegian Data Protection Authority (Datatilsynet), Norway’s supervisory authority (GDPR article 77), or with the supervisory authority of the country where you live or work. A decision of Datatilsynet can be appealed to the Privacy Appeals Board (Personvernnemnda).

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page concerns can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the register never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

changes.heading: Updates to this notice
body: This notice is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer admitted in Norway and by the data protection officer; every version is dated.

body: Pages are generated for the establishments the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities lists under the main industry codes of Statistics Norway’s standard (SN2025) for somatic hospitals (86.101), psychiatric hospitals and specialised addiction treatment (86.102, 86.103, 86.104), general practice (86.210, an emergency clinic told by its name), specialist medical practice (86.221, 86.222), dental practice (86.230), nursing homes (87.102) and pharmacies (47.730), kept as said above.

Not listed: health personnel, physiotherapists, psychologists, chiropractors, midwives and home nursing (which mostly work as sole proprietors), health centres for children and schools, ambulances, laboratories.

An establishment is placed at its address point in the cadastre (Kartverket). An address the cadastre does not know is placed at the centre of its postcode: its map position and its distance are then those of the postcode, never of the address.

kinds.NO_MENTAL_HEALTH: Mental health care and addiction treatment (district psychiatric centres, child and adolescent psychiatry)
kinds.NO_DENTAL: Dental clinics, public dental service included

PrivacyIe.metaDescription: Data processed by the Irish pages of Apercura: sources, purposes, legal bases, retention, recipients and your rights, including objection (GDPR articles 13, 14 and 21, Data Protection Act 2018).
PrivacyIe.title: Privacy notice
PrivacyIe.lead: What data the Irish pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The service provider named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of facility accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about facilities
body: Data: the facility's name as its register publishes it, its kind (pharmacy, nursing home, hospital, health centre), its address and Eircode, its town and county, its telephone number where the list gives one, for a hospital its kind as the HSE names it, for a nursing home its number of places for residents and the link to its page on HIQA's website, and who runs it when that is the HSE or a company. A facility that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Identifier: the PSI's registration number of the pharmacy, HIQA's centre number of the nursing home, or a key derived from a hospital's or health centre's county, name and address, at the end of the page's address.
Purpose: letting the public find a pharmacy, a nursing home, a hospital or a health centre, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.

Retention: as long as the facility is on its register or list. A page disappears at the import after the facility has left it (a pharmacy struck off the register, for example); a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the facilities themselves (GDPR article 14). This notice gives the information article 14 asks for, on the site where the pages are: the categories of data, their sources, the purposes and legal basis, the retention, the recipients and your rights, including the right to object. Every page links to it, and the data page lists the sources.

people.heading: Facilities, and the people they may name
body: An Irish page is a facility, never a person's profile. No register of individual doctors, nurses, pharmacists or other clinicians is imported, and the HSE's layer of GP practices, which names doctors, is not read.

A facility's details can still be about a person in three cases. A pharmacy's trading name may be a person's name (“Example's Pharmacy”): it is shown as the PSI's register publishes it, since another name would mislead. A nursing home's operator is shown only when it is the HSE or a company registered with the Companies Registration Office whose name names no person; an individual provider or a partnership is never stored. A facility's phone is its own line, but one that reaches a sole trader directly can be personal data.

Never read or stored, although the lists publish them: the owner of a pharmacy business, its superintendent and supervising pharmacists, a nursing home's person in charge and their phone, management contacts, the provider's own address and phone, and every email address. No rating and no review is collected.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Every page is built from a public register or open government data, re-used with the attribution each publisher asks for. The PSI must publish its registers on the Internet, free of charge (Pharmacy Act 2007, section 13); HIQA's registers of designated centres are open to inspection by the public and made available on the Internet (Health Act 2007, section 49(3)):

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: people need to know where the registered pharmacies, nursing homes, hospitals and health centres are and how to reach them, the need for which the law has the PSI and HIQA publish their registers on the Internet.

Necessity: only what identifies and reaches a facility is shown, as its register publishes it: its name, kind, address and phone. A pharmacy registered under a person's name cannot be listed under another without misleading; everything else that names a person is left out.

Balance: the same facts are on the public register and, for a pharmacy, on its shop front, so a facility listed by its regulator expects to be found in a directory repeating them. No special category of data, no rating, no review, no comparison, no paid placement; a neutral order; an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back; corrections at the source; pages that follow every import of the registers. Weighing these points, the interests of the public prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Facility accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right facility. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and the page concerned; for an “I run this facility” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a facility that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again. A holder who removes their page keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, kind and identifier shown in their space, their claim and the places their agenda uses, until the account is deleted.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in facilities and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; facility sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page's holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: The directory's pages are public. Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider's team and the processors below receive the other data, each for its own part. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor's IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Economic Area
body: The data is hosted and processed in the European Economic Area. Nothing is transferred outside it; any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can also lodge a complaint with the Data Protection Commission, Ireland's supervisory authority (GDPR article 77; Data Protection Act 2018, section 11): 6 Pembroke Row, Dublin 2, D02 X963, www.dataprotection.ie. The provider is established in France, so its lead supervisory authority is the Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL), with which you can lodge a complaint too: www.cnil.fr.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the imports of the registers never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

body: This notice is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer qualified in Ireland and by the data protection officer; every version is dated.

TermsIe.title: Terms of use
TermsIe.lead: The rules for using the Irish pages of Apercura, for the public and for facilities alike.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura lists, free of charge, the pharmacies on the Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland's register, the nursing homes on HIQA's register of designated centres for older people, and the hospitals and health centres of the HSE's Health Atlas. It is a directory only: no appointment is booked through Apercura in Ireland. It is run by the service provider named in the legal notice.
Using the directory requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from public registers and lists, as they publish it, in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement. No facility pays to be listed or to be shown first, and none is endorsed. They list facilities, never individual clinicians.

Each list has its own date: the PSI's register as of the date it gives, HIQA's register as of the last import, the HSE's hospitals and health centres as recorded in March 2020. The information may be incomplete or out of date: check it with the facility before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 112 or 999. Outside your GP's hours, contact the GP out-of-hours service for your area; a pharmacist can advise on minor illnesses.

facilities.heading: For facilities
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it, checked by a person before the page is handed over.
The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date, and must not advertise a product or service.

removal.heading: Correcting or removing a page
body: A fact taken from a register is corrected with the body that publishes it, and the page follows at the next import; anything else can be reported with the form on the data page. Anyone a page is about can ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information facilities add to their pages. Nothing in these terms limits a liability that the law does not allow to be limited, such as liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence. These terms will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. Directory data is re-used under the re-use conditions of the PSI and HIQA and under CC BY 4.0: the data page lists every source.

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: These terms are governed by French law, the law of the provider's establishment. If you use the site as a consumer living in Ireland, you keep the protection of the mandatory rules of Irish law and can bring a claim before the Irish courts. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution.

AccessibilityIe.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityIe.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the Irish pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: This statement is voluntary. The European Union (Accessibility of Websites and Mobile Applications of Public Sector Bodies) Regulations 2020 (S.I. No. 358 of 2020) bind public sector bodies, which Apercura is not, and the European Union (Accessibility Requirements of Products and Services) Regulations 2023 (S.I. No. 636 of 2023) bind the services they list, among them e-commerce services, which a free directory is not. Its provider nevertheless aims at the same standard on every page: WCAG 2.2 level AA.

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The Irish pages share the code of the other markets' pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress. The pages are in English only for now.

tests.heading: What was checked
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers.
A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within one month and, where needed, give you the information in another form.

DataIe.metaDescription: Where the Irish pages of Apercura come from: the PSI's register of pharmacies, HIQA's register of nursing homes, the HSE's Health Atlas layers and the places of Tailte Éireann and the CSO, with their terms, dates, what is not imported, and how to correct or remove a page.
DataIe.title: Data and sources
DataIe.lead: Every Irish page is built from a public register or open government data. Here is where it comes from, under which terms and attribution, how old each list is, what is left out and why, and how to correct or remove a page.

status.heading: Last update
status.body: The PSI publishes its register of pharmacies every month, and HIQA's register of nursing homes is exported as it stands on the day of each import. The directory imports a list when it has changed; a page changes only when its facts change in its list.
status.notImported: The Irish directory has not been imported yet on this site.

dates.heading: How old each list is
body: Each list is as old as its publisher's last edition, and the HSE's is old: its Health Atlas gave its layers of hospitals and health centres to GeoHive in March 2020, and no more recent open list of the HSE's facilities was found. The HSE's 2017 list on data.ehealthireland.ie is older still and can no longer be downloaded; the CSO's 2026 “Distance to Services” layers give distances to services, not a list of facilities. A hospital or health centre opened, renamed or closed since March 2020 is therefore missing or out of date here: its page says so.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.body: The PSI's and HIQA's registers are re-used under their publishers' re-use conditions; the HSE's layers and the places of Tailte Éireann and the CSO are published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0), which asks for the source to be credited. Each attribution below is printed word for word, and every Irish page prints those of its own sources.
sources.caption: Data sources of the Irish directory

ie-psi.use: Retail pharmacy businesses: names as registered, addresses, Eircodes, towns and counties, registration numbers

ie-hiqa.use: Designated centres for older people (nursing homes): names, addresses, Eircodes, counties, phone numbers, places for residents, the operator when it is the HSE or a company, the link to the centre's inspection reports
ie-hiqa.frequency: Exported from HIQA's register at each import

ie-hse-hospitals.use: Public, voluntary and private hospitals: names, addresses, kinds of hospital, points

ie-hse-health-centres.use: The HSE's health centres: names, addresses, points

ie-counties.use: The 26 counties, in which every facility is placed

ie-towns.use: The towns of the 2022 census (Built Up Areas), in which facilities are placed, and the point of each town

ie-placenames.use: The names of towns and villages, to match the town a list writes with the census's

map.name: Map data
map.use: The base map of the pages

conditions: The PSI's terms of use allow free re-use of its registers in any format, provided the source and its copyright are acknowledged, the information is reproduced accurately and not used in a misleading way, and the user agrees to “Not use the information for the principal purpose of advertising or promoting a particular product or service”. They refer to the latest PSI licence on data.gov.ie, today the Open Data Licence of data.gov.ie (CC BY 4.0), which does not cover personal data. HIQA's re-use conditions point to the same PSI licence.

Apercura's use fits these conditions: it is a free directory without advertising, which lists every registered pharmacy and nursing home the same way, in a neutral order, sells no placement or ranking, promotes no product or service, and links each page to the register it comes from. The rules on advertising that bind pharmacists (the PSI's guidance and code of conduct) and on advertising medicinal products (S.I. No. 541 of 2007) concern what a pharmacy or a supplier publishes: Apercura names no medicine, and no listing is paid for or endorsed.

coverage.heading: Facilities covered
body: A page is a facility, never a person. Ireland's pages list:

kinds.IE_PHARMACY: Pharmacies: every retail pharmacy business on the PSI's register
kinds.IE_NURSING_HOME: Nursing homes: every designated centre for older people on HIQA's register
kinds.IE_HOSPITAL: Hospitals: the public, voluntary and private hospitals of the HSE's Health Atlas, March 2020
kinds.IE_HEALTH_CENTRE: Health centres: the HSE's health centres of the Health Atlas, March 2020

excluded.heading: What is not imported, and why
body: Some data would complete the directory but cannot be re-used, or is not needed:
list: GP practices: the HSE's layer of GP practices names the doctors, so it is not read. No GP, dentist or other clinic is listed.

Health professionals: the registers of doctors (Medical Council), nurses and midwives (NMBI), dentists (Dental Council) and pharmacists (PSI) can be searched one entry at a time, but are not published for re-use. No person is listed.
HIQA's register of designated centres for people with disabilities: it gives no address of its centres.
OpenStreetMap: used for the base map only, never as a source of facilities or of their positions, since its Open Database Licence (ODbL) is share-alike.
Data about individuals, never: no register of people, no ratings, no reviews.

unread.heading: Fields never read
body: The lists hold some fields a page does not need, some of which name or reach a person. They are never read or stored:
list: The owner of a pharmacy business and its superintendent and supervising pharmacists, in the PSI's register.

A nursing home's person in charge and their phone, its management contacts, and the provider's own address and phone, in HIQA's register; the provider's name only when it is the HSE or a company whose name names no person.
Email addresses, in every list.

locations.heading: Locations
body: Every facility is placed in its county, from Tailte Éireann's boundaries, and in its town, from the CSO's Built Up Areas of the 2022 census, by the town and county its list writes. A facility whose town is not one of the census's is placed in its county only: it appears in its county's listing.

Eircodes are printed as part of an address, as the lists publish them, but never used to locate a facility: the Eircode database is not open data. A pharmacy or a nursing home is shown at the point of its town: no pin marks it on a map, and its distance is approximate. A hospital or health centre is shown at the point the HSE's layer gives it, as recorded in March 2020.

identifiers.heading: Identifiers
body: The address of every page ends with a key, after a letter naming its list, so that a page can be found and checked against its source:
list: /ie/facility/example-pharmacy-p1234: the PSI's registration number of a pharmacy, after p.
/ie/facility/example-nursing-home-n738: HIQA's centre number of a nursing home, after n.
/ie/facility/example-hospital-h123456789: the HSE's layer numbers no hospital, so its key is derived from its county, name and address, after h; a health centre's follows c.

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the public registers: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import after the corrected list is published.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: A pharmacy: the pharmacy business tells the Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland, which keeps its register.
A nursing home: the registered provider tells HIQA, which keeps the register of designated centres.
A hospital or health centre: the HSE's March 2020 layers are not published again; report the error with the form below.
Phone, website and opening hours: where the list gives none, a facility adds them by claiming its page.

An unclaimed page is hidden as soon as the request arrives and deleted after a light check; it never comes back with the imports of the registers. A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space. Every page also has its own removal form.
